summary.text: A 23-year-old woman with a history of medullary thyroid cancer (T3N1bM0), treated by thyroidectomy, and no family history of thyroid disease, thyroid cancer or other cancers, was referred to neurosurgery three months later after routine neck CT imaging showed a fourth ventricular mass. She reported intermittent headaches, denied motor weakness, gait, vision and swallowing issues and dizziness, and had no focal neurological deficits.

Calcitriol had declined from above 9000 to 16 pg/mL, free T4 was normal and TSH slightly elevated at 4.5 uiu/mL, treated with daily levothyroxine. MRI showed a lobular mass at the obex of the fourth ventricle; complete neuroaxis imaging showed no additional lesions. The differential included ependymoma, CPP, choroid plexus carcinoma, subependymoma, meningioma, medulloblastoma, astrocytoma and hemangioblastoma.

She underwent an elective suboccipital craniotomy and C1 laminectomy for tumor resection. Histopathology showed a papillary neoplasm with scattered microcalcifications, positive for glial fibrillary acidic protein, transthyretin and CK7, most consistent with choroid plexus papilloma. Postoperative MRI demonstrated gross total resection. Tumor exome sequencing found no somatic mutations unique to the tumor; germline testing was negative for RET and TP53 and found a heterozygous CDH1 variant of uncertain significance.

At 36-month postthyroidectomy and 33-month postcraniotomy there was no recurrence of CPP or medullary thyroid cancer. Additional nodules of undetermined significance were identified in the liver, vertebral column and lung, all lesions were stable over 1 year, and continued surveillance was planned. Calcitriol and thyroid panel testing remain normal.
